subsystems.name: Thermal protection system
subsystems.role: a sun-facing shield that keeps the rest of the spacecraft in shadow while solar flux reaches tens to hundreds of times the intensity at Earth.

subsystems.name: Spacecraft bus
subsystems.role: carries the payload in permanent shade and survives the huge temperature difference between the sunlit and dark sides.

subsystems.name: Kick stage
subsystems.role: the engine that fires once at perihelion, where the Oberth effect turns each kilogram of propellant into the largest possible speed gain.

subsystems.name: Power source
subsystems.role: supplies electricity for years of cruise far from the Sun, when the shield geometry leaves no room for solar arrays.
parts: radioisotope thermoelectric generator or Stirling unit

subsystems.name: Communications and navigation
subsystems.role: reports science data and stays oriented, including through a solar conjunction when the shield must face the Sun and the antenna cannot point at Earth.
parts: autonomous star trackers and inertial sensors

subsystems.name: Science payload
subsystems.role: measures the outer heliosphere, Kuiper Belt or planetary targets at the end of the fast transit.

buildSteps.title: Design the trajectory
buildSteps.detail: Choose a perihelion radius — typically well inside 0.2 AU — and a Jupiter flyby that pumps the orbit inward, then back out, balancing heat load against speed gained.

buildSteps.title: Model the thermal environment
buildSteps.detail: Computer models and vacuum-chamber tests reproduce the solar flux and infrared re-radiation the shield and bus will face at closest approach.

buildSteps.title: Make the heat shield
buildSteps.detail: Carbon-carbon composite facesheets are bonded to a carbon foam core and coated with a bright ceramic layer so most incident energy is reflected, not absorbed.

buildSteps.title: Build and shade the bus
buildSteps.detail: Components are mounted so the shield casts a shadow over the whole spacecraft, with radiators on the dark side and every gap closed against stray light.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the kick stage
buildSteps.detail: The motor is attached and tested for ignition after years of cold soak, since it must fire on the first attempt with no margin for a retry.

buildSteps.title: Test end to end
buildSteps.detail: Launch vibration, thermal-vacuum and electromagnetic testing verify the spacecraft before shipping to the launch site.

buildSteps.title: Launch and fly the gravity assists
buildSteps.detail: After launch, Earth and Jupiter flybys shrink the orbit until the probe is falling sunward on the planned path.

buildSteps.title: Burn at perihelion
buildSteps.detail: The motor fires near closest approach, adding speed where the spacecraft is moving fastest; the shield is hottest and communications may be interrupted.

buildSteps.title: Coast outbound
buildSteps.detail: The probe cruises to its target with the payload active, then transmits data across a much shorter mission lifetime than conventional outer-planet missions.

prerequisites.tech: Solar heat shields demonstrated in flight
prerequisites.why: Parker Solar Probe has survived passes inside 0.05 AU behind a roughly 11 cm carbon-composite shield, but its instruments stay behind the shield rather than operating a full spacecraft through the encounter.
flybys of Jupiter have been used repeatedly to reshape spacecraft orbits, including dropping a probe's perihelion toward the Sun.
they are the only mature way to power a spacecraft for years beyond Jupiter, though they must be kept cool during the hot solar pass.

prerequisites.tech: High-thrust upper stages that survive long storage
prerequisites.why: the perihelion burn happens years after launch, so the motor must ignite reliably after a long, cold, unattended coast.
light travel time and a possible communications blackout mean the spacecraft must hold attitude and trigger the burn without ground control.

pathway.milestone: conceptual mission studies, such as the interstellar-probe design work carried out for NASA, plus Parker Solar Probe's progressively closer passes
pathway.unlocks: data on how materials and electronics behave in extreme solar flux.

pathway.milestone: a dedicated technology demonstration of a perihelion burn
pathway.unlocks: confidence that a motor can be stored for years and fired reliably in that environment.

pathway.milestone: a first Solar Oberth probe to the outer heliosphere or Kuiper Belt
pathway.unlocks: arrival times several times shorter than gravity-assist-only missions allow.
routine rapid access to distant targets, and a credible precursor path toward an interstellar probe.
